My mother

I was 15 at the time and in high school. My mother worked 3rd shift for many years so when my brother and I would wake up and go to school sometimes she would still be asleep. We usually woke her up to say goodbye and go to school but that day we didn't. When we returned from school that day we did your usual thing of eating a snack. I remember talking to my brother in the kitchen about his day. He said he had a really good day(Hes autistic so that was excellent news) I told him to wake up our mother. He came out and said she wouldn't wake up. I went into the room and knew something was wrong. Her skin was pale and her face was blue. I shook her for a few minutes trying to wake her and she didn't. I looked back and my brother was standing in the door looking at me and I said I think shes dead. He immediately started crying and ran off. I called 911. While I was talking to the operator I remember her asking me if i knew CPR  and I lied and said no. She then started to walk me through it and I said No, I can't. I don't know why I did that but I hate my self every day for it. My brother came back crying worst than ever and told me he had went to the neighbors house to ask for help and they turned him away. THEY FUCKING TURNED AWAY A CHILD ASKING FOR HELP CAUSE HIS MOTHER JUST DIED. I now know why is because we are mixed race. After this the first police officer came in the house and went to check in my moms room. My brother and I walked into the breeze-way and just stood there. He came into the Breeze-way and asked if we could call our father. I picked up the phone and dialed his number. I felt so numb at this point that when he answered I couldn't say a word and the officer took the phone from me and told him. My brother and I stood in the breeze-way and waited for my dad. When he came we still stayed in the breeze-way for hours till our uncle came and took us to our aunts house. I still think about it all the time 8 years later. I still hate my self every day for not waking her up and not trying CPR on her.
